title: [ROCm][TunableOp] Simple matmul with TunableOp results in segfault

labels.name: module: crash
labels.description: Problem manifests as a hard crash, as opposed to a RuntimeError

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Running the example matmul with TunableOp enabled from the [official AMD blog post](https://rocm.blogs.amd.com/artificial-intelligence/pytorch-tunableop/README.html) results in a segfault.

Code:

```python
import torch


def time_matmul(M, N, K):
    n_iter = 10000  # Number of iterations to time
    n_warmup = 10  # Number of warmup iterations

    t0 = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    t1 = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)

    # Construct input matrices
    A = torch.rand(M, K, device="cuda")
    B = torch.rand(K, N, device="cuda")

    # Benchmark the GEMM
    for i in range(n_iter + n_warmup):
        if i == n_warmup:
            t0.record()  # Don't start recording until warmup is finished
        C = A @ B

    # Compute elapsed time
    t1.record()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    dt = t0.elapsed_time(t1) / 1000

    print(f"{n_iter/dt:0.2f} iter/s ({dt:0.4g}s)")


time_matmul(512, 1024, 2048)
```

Run with:
```shell
PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_ENABLED=1 PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_VERBOSE=1 PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_FILENAME=matmul_result.csv python3 matmul.py
```

Tested on a 1x MI300X. The same code on NVIDIA works as expected.
